simple: Roblox keeps old saved and published versions of each place, and Version History is where you see them. You can write notes on a save, like "added the boss room", so you can find it later, and you can go back to an older version if something breaks. This is your safety net: if a change ruins your game, you can return to a version that worked.
analogy: It is like save slots in a video game. Before a hard boss you make a save named "before boss", and if things go badly you load it and try again.
keyPoints: Open the Version History widget from Window > Version History. You can dock it anywhere in Studio.
You can search your version notes and filter by date, auto or manual save, published saves, collaborator, and whether a save has notes.
To save with notes, use File > Save to Roblox with Notes, or press Ctrl+Alt+S (Windows) or Cmd+Option+S (Mac).
Notes are required when you publish, so you always know what changed for players.
Studio can draft publish notes by summarizing your team's version notes since the last publish. You can edit, keep, or dismiss the draft.
To restore in Studio: open Version History, click the three-dot menu on a version, Open Local Copy, then File > Save to Roblox As and overwrite the place.
To restore on the Creator Dashboard: your game > Configurations > Places > pick the place > Version History > Restore.
Restoring creates a new version but does not publish it. For a public game, publish it and restart servers so players get it.

terms.version: One saved snapshot of your place at a certain moment.
terms.checkpoint: A version you mark as important, like a finished level, so you can easily return to it.
terms.version notes: A name and description you attach to a save, like "v1.2: new shop".
terms.auto save vs manual save: An auto save happens on its own every few minutes. A manual save is one you made yourself.
terms.widget: A small window inside Studio that you can move and dock.
terms.dock: Snap a window into a spot in your Studio layout so it stays there.
terms.restore: Bring back an older version. It is added as a brand-new version, so the newer ones are not erased.
terms.roll back: Go back to an earlier version that worked.
terms.local copy: A copy opened on your computer that is not yet saved to Roblox.

watchOut: Restoring a version and thinking players now have it. You still have to publish it and restart servers.
Saving without notes all the time. Later you will not know which save is which. Add a short note for big changes.
Searching for notes on very old saves. Versions from before this feature existed cannot be searched until you add notes to them.
